Author: Krishan Pahal

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mani Shankar
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Satyendra Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Mani Shankar,
learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Anit Kumar Shukla, learned A.G.A. for the State and
perused the material placed on record.

2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 25 of 2024, U/S 506 Ipc and 5H/6 of Pocso Act, Police
Station Kotwali, District Maharajganj, during the pendency of trial.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:

3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has already been granted bail by another Bench of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 26443 of 2024 Mithlesh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95803189/
1 vide order dated 29.8.2024 u/s 376, 452, 506 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 26443 of 2024 Mithlesh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After investigation, the investigating officer has submitted the final report (charge sheet) in the added section 5H/6 of POCSO Act and 506 IPC also, as such, the applicant is entitled for bail in the added sections as well.
4. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
5. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.1.2024
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application but has not disputed the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant.

CONCLUSION:
7. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.
8. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
9.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
10. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
11. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

12. In the judgments of the Supreme Court passed in case of Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth vs. State of Gujarat & Another reported in 2016 (1) SCC (Cri) 240 and Manoj Suresh Jadhav & Ors. vs. The State of Maharashtra, reported in 2018 SCC OnLine SC 3428, the applicant therein was enlarged on Mithlesh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95803189/
2

sentences.text: anticipatory bail in the added sections U/S 438 Cr.P.C. after being enlarged on regular bail U/S 439 Cr.P.C.
Although the instant case is of regular bail, but it can be considered to be at a better footing.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Mithlesh involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
15. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

16. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
